$comment: Every architecture rule Broiler.VM names, with how much it currently proves.
Milestone VM-1's exit gate asks that the contract be implemented and proven against the
fixture profile. A rule can be expressed long before the checkout contains anything able to
violate it, and a register that did not say so would let a passing suite read as stronger
evidence than it is. Roadmap section 16 makes an untruthful support claim a stop condition and
the status ledger's update rule 4 forbids promoting a shell result, so every rule carries its
status and the evidence bundle repeats the counts.
ONE CRITERION, APPLIED TO EVERY ROW. `status` describes the GRAPH: can anything in the current
checkout violate this rule? `witness` records a real violating input, and every rule has one
regardless of status - a Vacuous rule is one nothing in the component can break, not one that
was never shown working.
Status values, and nothing else: Active, Vacuous, Deferred.
Active   - something in the checkout could violate it, and a witness shows it rejecting one.
Vacuous  - it runs and is witnessed, but nothing in the graph can violate it. Not a defect:
the honest state of a rule whose subject cannot yet be broken.
Deferred - not asserted; the activation milestone owns promoting it.
A Deferred or Vacuous row may never name an activation milestone at or before the current
milestone, and a rule whose activation milestone IS the current milestone must be Active with a
passing witness. RuleRegisterTests enforces the register against the test methods and the
witness inputs in both directions.
WHAT VM-1 CHANGED. Five of the six rows that named VM-1 as their activation milestone are
promoted: the product graph now has method bodies, assembly references and an exported surface,
so B2, B4, B5b, B6 and B7 each have something that could break them. B3 is the one row where
the honest answer is different, and it is recorded rather than papered over - see its own row.
Rule E5 is superseded: it fused a cardinality claim about the graph with a member claim about
one type, and only the first is falsified by VM-1. V1 replaces the first; V2 preserves the
second verbatim.

REVIEW PASS. An adversarial review after the first implementation returned 45 findings that survived refutation, 16 of them blockers. Two register rows were among them: V4 checked a property count rather than the frozen rows it claimed to check, and V9 asserted static return types rather than the construction site. Both statements and both rules were corrected here. A rule weaker than its own statement is the defect this register exists to prevent, so those two are recorded rather than quietly tightened.

GROUP H, THE HUMAN-REVIEW RECORD RULES. The review documents - HUMAN_REVIEW.md, the worksheets under docs/review/, the evidence-bundle READMEs and the status ledger - carry marks, identifiers and figures, and every one of them is a claim about something else in the checkout. Unbound they rot, and this component has already found a transposed byte figure and two stale test counts in its own review record. H1 closes the mark vocabulary against the legend, H2 holds every cited exclusion to a definition in a bundle's exclusion table, H3 holds the review route to a fixed enumeration of eight areas and to the worksheet's own counts, H4 refuses an approval recorded over an unfilled attestation, and H5 binds every quoted headline figure to the log the bundle retains for it.

Group H replaces a group R that was written and reverted, for two reasons that are recorded rather than forgotten. First, R1..R6 is a reserved namespace: ADR 0003 records that R1..R6 are ADR 0012's six ownership roles, and renames another set away from R1..R5 for exactly that reason. H is unused across every record and the roadmap. Second, every rule in that attempt was weaker than its own statement, and an adversarial pass broke all five by editing the tree and watching the suite stay green - a capped token regex, a definition scanner that accepted any table row, an area set derived from the document under test, an attestation field list read off whatever bullets were present, and an image-size check that passed when the two sizes were exchanged. Each of those is named in the rule's own remarks and carries its own witness. Group H witnesses are per CLAUSE, not per rule: the single worst defect of the reverted attempt was asserting every witness with a bare non-empty check over an input that violated several clauses at once, which pinned only whichever clause fired first and let four independent clauses be deleted in one patch.

All five name owningAdr 0012, which owns the support-claim and ownership surface they protect. That is a NOMINAL owner and the only such row in this register: ADR 0012 is frozen and names none of them, while every other row names a record that states its rule. Exclusion EX-53 records it rather than letting the field imply a binding that does not exist.

A SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS, AGAINST GROUP H ITSELF. Three reviewers attacked the five rules by constructing violating inputs, running the suite and recording what stayed green; every escape they found is closed here or recorded as a limit. Four shapes recurred and are worth naming, because they are shapes and not one-off slips. A section lookup that returned its first match and never asked whether it was the only one made every rule readable from a decoy heading, which is how an APPROVED record over four unsigned attestation fields passed; sections are now required to be unique. A markdown reader that gated on the leading pipe, or on the absence of a block quote, put whole rows and whole list items outside every rule that read them. A definition scanner told to read a section rather than a TABLE accepted anything appended to the end of a bundle, code fences included. And a clause with no witness of its own is a clause that can be deleted in the same patch as three others with nothing red - which is why every phrasing, every enumeration member and every placeholder word now has an input that names it. The register's own witness column was among the findings: exchanging two rows' witness fields wholesale satisfied every check that read them, so a witness named for a rule is now held to the row it sits in, and the orphan check compares whole paths rather than asking whether some row's witness string contained the file name.

GROUP J, THE CODE-ASSURANCE RULES. Every product unit now carries the policy's two-line review block, every generated header and CODE-ASSURANCE.md is written from those blocks, and NOTHING in this component has been reviewed by a human. Group J is what keeps that record honest in both directions. J1 holds coverage to the exemption predicate, J2 holds every field to its closed vocabulary and reports a block that parses as nothing, J3 binds each recorded fingerprint to the declaration it describes, J4 refuses any approval a human did not make, and J5 holds every generated artefact to what the generator would write. The letter J was chosen because A-E, V, F, M, G, P, S and T are in use, H is group R's replacement, and R1..R6 is the reserved namespace ADR 0003 records for ADR 0012's six ownership roles.

J4 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The value of this system at VM-1 is that it records the ABSENCE of review precisely; a mechanism that could turn PENDING into a name would convert an honest record of no review into a false one, and a false record is worse than none because it is trusted. The policy states that prohibition as a sentence about CI. Here it is an exception the generator throws, four separately witnessed transitions, and an assertion over the rendered text of every artefact rather than over the model that produced it.

Group J witnesses are per CLAUSE, like group H's and for the same reason: a witness asserted with a bare non-empty check pins only whichever clause fires first, and four independent clauses can then be deleted in one patch with nothing red. Every assertion here names the CONTENT of the violation it expects. Forty witness inputs sit under witnesses/assurance/, and several of them carry the reviewer identifier WITNESS-ONLY, which is not a person and appears nowhere else - a rule about false approvals cannot be witnessed without an input that contains one.

Three limits are recorded as exclusions rather than left implied, one per rule that has one: EX-60, that no CI lane runs either mode, so the policy's CI-enforcement clause is unmet; EX-61, that a six-hex fingerprint answers only whether a unit changed and is neither collision-free across units nor a cryptographic commitment; and EX-62, that the exemption predicate decides relevance, so a unit it wrongly exempts is invisible to J1.

All five rows name owningAdr 0012, and that is NOMINAL, exactly as group H's is. ADR 0012 owns who is allowed to say yes and what may be said in public, which is this system's subject; it is frozen and names none of these rules. EX-53 is extended to cover both groups rather than duplicated.

rules.statement: No ProjectReference, resolved to a full path, lies outside the component root.

rules.statement: No PackageReference names a Broiler.* package.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Any project file exists; closes the feed-shaped reintroduction A1 cannot see.

rules.statement: No Compile, None, Content, EmbeddedResource or Import item resolves outside the component root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Non-vacuous when any project declares one of the five item types; at VM-0 none does, so the sweep is empty and both witnesses carry the rule.

rules.statement: No product project has a ProjectReference resolving under src/tests/.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures exists at VM-0, so the forbidden target is present.

rules.statement: Every project under src/tests/ contains the literal element IsPackable false.
rules.evidence: Project file text, not the evaluated property
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures matches no name-suffix rule in the vendored packaging props and would otherwise default to packable.

rules.statement: Exactly three projects declare a PackageId, and for each PackageId equals AssemblyName equals RootNamespace equals the project file base name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three packable projects exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: The resolved ProjectReference edge multiset equals graph.manifest.json exactly; extra and missing edges both fail. Subsumes acyclicity.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Eight edges exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: No profile project references Broiler.VM.Runtime.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Fixtures is profile-shaped and exists at VM-0.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Runtime declares OutputType Library or omits it, and declares no composition root.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Runtime exists at VM-0.

rules.statement: No product project declares InternalsVisibleTo. VM-3 must prove a profile is writable through the public source contract alone.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three product projects exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: No project outside the composition-root allow-list references an assembly matching Broiler.VM.Profile.*. The allow-list is empty at VM-0.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The allow-list is empty at VM-0, so any profile reference violates it.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary reference nothing outside the framework. The mechanical form of roadmap section 5's arrow to nothing.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Both assemblies are built at VM-0; the test assembly is the witness input.

rules.statement: Broiler.VM.Runtime references nothing outside Broiler.VM.Abstractions and Broiler.VM.Binary.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Broiler.VM.Runtime now uses types from both Abstractions and Binary - its meter implements Broiler.VM.IVmBoundedAllocationMeter and its verification path drives VmBoundedReader - so its AssemblyRef table names both and the rule is equality rather than subset.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph names a Broiler.* assembly outside the component's own set. The assembly-level twin of A1 and A2.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A product assembly could name a foreign Broiler.* assembly. The subject now exists - the product graph names non-framework assemblies for the first time - but a VIOLATION is still unreachable: A1 forbids the outbound ProjectReference, A2 forbids the Broiler.* PackageReference, and the single-source NuGet.config makes such a package unresolvable, so no project in the checkout can acquire one. It becomes reachable at VM-3, when composition roots and profile packages exist. Exclusion EX-40 records the reasoning and the alternative that was rejected.
rules.witness: none - a witness needs a foreign Broiler assembly, and the graph is closed over its own seven. The project-file twins A1 and A2 are witnessed.

rules.statement: No exported member of a product assembly names a type outside System.* and Broiler.VM.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a contract surface whose members carry parameter and return types, so a foreign type on the public surface is now expressible.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph references a dynamic-loading, reflection-invocation or IL-emit API. Invariant 2 requires registration to be static and typed.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The witness is compiled into the test assembly, which the same scanner flags when pointed at it.

rules.statement: No assembly in the product graph applies ModuleInitializerAttribute. Invariant 2 forbids a module-initializer ordering dependency by name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph now declares method bodies, so a method could carry the attribute.

rules.statement: No product assembly references an assembly built from src/tests/.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: ApiBaselineWitnesses.FixtureReferenceWitness names a type from Broiler.VM.Fixtures - which is built from src/tests/ - so the test assembly emits the AssemblyRef the rule scans for. A project reference alone emits nothing: the compiler records only what is used, so without a real use the scanner would be pointed at an assembly that does not in fact hold the forbidden edge.

rules.statement: No product assembly exports a type named BuiltInProfiles, DefaultProfiles, AllProfiles or KnownProfiles. Roadmap section 3 rejects an aggregate profile type by name.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports types other than VmCoreContract, so an aggregate profile type is now expressible.

rules.statement: dotnet pack over Broiler.VM.slnx produces exactly three .nupkg and three .snupkg, named for the three product assemblies.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists. VM-0 creates no CI workflow; a manually executed pack log is retained in the evidence bundle as observed state, not as a rule assertion.

rules.statement: No produced .nuspec declares a dependency on a Broiler.* package outside the declared three.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists.

rules.statement: No produced .nuspec's id, title, description, tags or release notes names a language. Implements roadmap section 14's packaging failure 'a language capability implied by package or API'.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: A component CI pack step exists.

rules.statement: No project file outside the component declares a ProjectReference or PackageReference resolving into Broiler.VM. The inbound half of the legacy boundary.
rules.evidence: Project files in an aggregate checkout above the component
rules.nonVacuousWhen: An aggregate checkout is present above the component root. Where none is, the rule reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than passing. Exclusion EX-01 records the conditionality.

rules.statement: VmCoreContract.Version and VmCoreContract.MinimumSupportedVersion equal the values in ADR 0003's header fields.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: ADR 0003 and VmCoreContract both exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: Every ADR file declares a Core contract header field, and the contract-bearing set is exactly 0002 through 0011.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Twelve ADR files exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: Every contract-bearing ADR declares the current core contract version.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Ten contract-bearing ADRs exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: The ADR index lists exactly the ADR files present, and every rule identifier named in an ADR has exactly one row in this register.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Twelve ADR files and this register exist at VM-0.

rules.statement: SUPERSEDED AT VM-1 by V1 and V2. As written it fused a cardinality claim about the graph (exactly one public type) with a member claim about one type (whose only members are the two contract-version constants). VM-1 necessarily falsifies the first and preserves the second. V1 replaces the cardinality half with an API baseline; V2 preserves the member half verbatim. The row is retained rather than removed so the supersession is auditable, and it asserts nothing.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Never again in this form; VM-6 owns removing the row when it freezes the public API.

rules.statement: The product graph exports every name the frozen public-name table fixes, and every exported type is declared in namespace Broiler.VM.
rules.evidence: Exported types against the frozen name baseline
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a contract surface. Replaces the cardinality half of E5. The witness points the rule at a graph exporting only the bounded-reading primitives which contains none of the frozen names.

rules.statement: VmCoreContract exports exactly Version and MinimumSupportedVersion, and both are literals.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmCoreContract exists. Preserves the member half of E5 verbatim.

rules.statement: No exported type or member uses a retired name, a struck bound name, or one of the six unqualified names the terminology rule bans.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a surface on which a retired name could appear.

rules.statement: VmProfileDescriptor declares exactly the thirty rows of the frozen table, by name, and none of the names excluded by construction.
rules.evidence: Compiled metadata against the frozen row list
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The descriptor exists as a type with properties. The rule compares row NAMES, not a count: a count is satisfied by any thirty-one properties at all, including thirty-one wrong ones, which is exactly the drift a table this long exists to catch.

rules.statement: Every reason in the registry maps to exactly one outcome category, derivably from its own value.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmReason and VmReasonRegistry exist. The witness is a reason value filed outside every category block which the derived mapping must reject.

rules.statement: The profile-facing metering surface declares exactly TryCharge, Poll, ReportRetained and ReportReleased, the charge amount is unsigned, and no member reads a remaining or effective value.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: IVmMeter exists.

rules.statement: No member on any exported type is named Grant, Refund, Reset, Extend, Increase, Raise, TopUp, Widen, Reopen, WithLimits, Withdraw or Credit.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports members on which such a name could appear.

rules.statement: No public member returns Task, ValueTask or IAsyncEnumerable, and no product assembly calls a timer, delay or thread-abort API.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports members with return types and declares method bodies.

rules.statement: Exactly one public member of the product graph mints a verified artifact, exactly one product assembly reaches that member, and the verification member takes exactly the descriptor, the byte span and a cancellation token.
rules.evidence: Compiled metadata: exported members, MemberRef tables, and the verification signature
rules.nonVacuousWhen: VmVerifiedArtifact and VmRuntime.Verify exist. Two halves, because either alone is weaker than the claim: counting members that return the handle would pass a graph with one factory and any number of assemblies calling it, and reading the member-reference tables says which assemblies can reach the factory at all. Neither half counts individual call sites, which would need an IL decoder; Exclusion EX-51 records that limit rather than letting the statement overreach.

rules.statement: No public member can express a persisted envelope, streaming or incremental verification, lazy per-section verification, or in-process producer input.
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product graph exports a surface on which such a member could appear.

rules.statement: Every mark token in a review document is one of the nine the legend publishes, and the legend publishes exactly those nine, once each. A mark token is a table cell whose whole trimmed text is bracketed, a bracketed token leading a list item, or the final token of an ATX heading - with or without backticks, and inside a block quote or not.
rules.evidence: HUMAN_REVIEW.md, docs/review/*.md, docs/evidence/*/README.md and docs/roadmap.status.md against a hard-coded set of nine
rules.nonVacuousWhen: All five review documents exist and carry marks in all three positions. The nine are hard-coded, never read from the document, and the legend is parsed independently of the body scan so that a tenth mark added to the legend is visible to the equality check. The token pattern carries NO length cap: capping it at six characters let [APPROVED], [REJECTED], [NOT MET] and [PENDING] through, which are the tokens an author actually reaches for. Rows are read with or without the optional leading pipe and with or without the optional trailing pipe, because GFM makes both optional and it is the delimiter row rather than either pipe that makes a table a table; gating the scan on the leading pipe let a whole row - a tenth legend mark among them - be skipped by dropping one character. Block-quote markers are stripped before a line is classified, so a quoted list item, table row or heading is still what it is; HUMAN_REVIEW.md opens with a quoted banner, so that is the document set's own idiom. Fenced code is not scanned, because an example is an illustration and not a claim. One carve-out, and only one: a GFM task-list checkbox - an unbackticked [ ], [x] or [X] leading a list item - is not a mark, because HUMAN_REVIEW.md section 1 rules that section 9's four-state decision list is written as ordinary markdown checkboxes and deliberately does not use this vocabulary. A bracketed token leading a list item in any other spelling is still a mark. No review document currently carries a mark in a heading, so both halves of that clause - backticked and bare - are carried by their witnesses alone.

rules.statement: Every EX- identifier cited in a review document is defined by a row of the section 9 exclusion table of an evidence bundle, or by a bolded list item in that section. A row of any OTHER table in section 9, a row in a subsection appended to section 9, and a row inside a fenced code block define nothing.
rules.evidence: The review documents against docs/evidence/*/README.md section 9
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Thirty-two exclusions are defined across the two bundles and cited from all five review documents. That figure had already drifted - it read twenty-six against a checkout carrying twenty-nine - and it is a count of a checkout rather than of a log, which is why nothing asserts it and why it is stated here rather than relied upon. Only the exclusion table defines, and only in section 9. A bundle also carries a gate table, an errata table, a negative-control table and a hash table, and accepting any table row whose first cell is an EX- identifier would let any of them launder an undefined citation; the table's own header is what decides, so a table that does not name an ID column and an Exclusion column defines nothing. Section 9 is the LAST section of a bundle and a section runs to the next heading at its own level or above, so being inside section 9 is not enough on its own: definitions stop at the first subheading, which is what keeps an errata or hash subsection appended to the end of the file out, and a fenced code block is not read at all, which is what stops a worked example minting the identifier it illustrates. The citation pattern accepts one digit as well as two, so EX-4 written for EX-04 - the commonest way this citation goes wrong - is reported rather than silently ignored, and it does not require a word boundary in front of the E, because an underscore is a word character and an anchored pattern could not see the italicised _EX-04_ at all. A citation inside a fenced code block is not read either, for the same reason a definition there is not: the two halves of the rule read the same document.

rules.statement: HUMAN_REVIEW.md declares exactly RA-1 through RA-8 in its route table and again in its area-verdict table, each area once; every area has at least one worksheet item; every item names one of the eight and names the area of the heading it sits under; item identifiers run contiguously from RC-01 with no gaps, no duplicates, no missing Area row and no repeated one; the worksheet's own per-area counts and total are true; and the item count HUMAN_REVIEW.md states is the number of items the worksheet carries. Every section either document is read through must be unique.
rules.evidence: HUMAN_REVIEW.md sections 4 and 8 against a fixed enumeration, and docs/review/vm-0-vm-1.md against itself and against the count HUMAN_REVIEW.md section 4 states
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Eight areas and fifty-three items exist. The eight are a fixed enumeration in the test and are never derived from the document under test: deriving them let RA-8 be deleted from the route table, the verdict table, the worksheet heading and its six items with the suite still green, which is structurally the same defect as the V4 one this register was created to prevent. Fixing the enumeration was not enough on its own, because every section this rule reads is found by a heading pattern: a lookup that returned its FIRST match let a full decoy route table inserted above the real one become the table under test while RA-8 was deleted from the real one, and a decoy Progress heading hid a falsified total the same way, so each section is required to be unique. TWO LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. First, the ITEM COUNT is not an enumeration and cannot be, because the worksheet grows: it is held by agreement between HUMAN_REVIEW.md and the worksheet, so no single-document edit can shed an item, but a coordinated edit to both still can and nothing outside the two documents says how many items the review ought to have. That is EX-55. Second, the worksheet's per-area counts and total are compared with the worksheet itself and with nothing else; what binds them outward is the eight-area enumeration and the stated total, not the counts.

rules.statement: HUMAN_REVIEW.md records exactly one decision, in exactly one decision section, and if that decision is anything other than PENDING then every one of the four attestation fields - Name, Reviewer alias, Signature or attributable commit, Date - is present, non-empty, carries at least one letter or digit, and is not a placeholder.
rules.evidence: HUMAN_REVIEW.md sections 9 and 11 against a fixed enumeration of four field names
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The decision list and the attestation both exist, and the decision is currently PENDING with every field unfilled - which is the honest state and which the rule must not reject. The field set is held to the fixed enumeration, so a MISSING field is a violation: reading whatever bullets happened to be present made deleting the signature line as good as filling it, and the cheapest possible way to record a false approval was the one path the rule could not see. Each of the four names, and each of the eight placeholder words, is exercised by a witness of its own, so neither list can shrink with the suite green. Both markdown italic forms are placeholders, because *not yet signed* renders identically to _not yet signed_; and because a closed word list cannot enumerate every way of writing nothing, a value with no letter and no digit in it - a bare hyphen, say - is refused on its own terms. The decision and attestation sections are each required to be unique: a decoy heading above the real one, carrying a ticked PENDING box, was enough to make an APPROVED record over four unsigned fields pass. What FILLED still does not mean is verified - a field carrying a plausible but invented name or commit is accepted, and no rule can tell otherwise. This is the false-approval risk ADR 0001 named when it deferred HUMAN_REVIEW.md to VM-6.

rules.statement: Every headline figure a review document quotes in a recognised phrasing matches the value in the log the evidence bundle retains for it: a suite total against the per-assembly Passed: totals in test.log or their sum, an architecture/behavioural split against the assembly each total names and in either word order, a Native AOT size against publish-aot.log, and a trimmed size against publish-jit-and-trimmed.log. The corpus must quote the current suite total, its split, its native image size and its trimmed image size at least once each, compared by value. A figure worded outside the recognised phrasings is not checked at all (EX-56). The rule checks document against LOG and not log against checkout: a stale log and a stale document agree with each other, and the bundle's expiry and recertification triggers are what cover that case (EX-54).
rules.evidence: The review documents against docs/evidence/vm-1/test.log, publish-aot.log and publish-jit-and-trimmed.log; a bundle README is compared against its own bundle's logs
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Three logs are retained and five documents quote figures from them. Each figure is bound to its own log and the split is bound per assembly, so exchanging the two image sizes - the likeliest form of this error, since the two numbers sit two lines apart in one sentence - fails twice rather than passing a set-membership check, and exchanging the two halves of the split fails whichever way round the halves are written. The four anti-deletion guards compare values; comparing patterns alone let the real figures be deleted while the VM-0 bundle's historical 35 passed kept the pattern alive, and the trimmed size had no guard at all, so nothing forced the corpus to keep quoting it once it had been reworded. TWO LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED. First, the phrasing lists are finite and a figure worded outside them is not checked at all. They are kept minimal and non-overlapping and every entry is exercised by a witness sentence no other entry matches, so no entry can be deleted silently and no entry is decoration; what they do not cover is a genuine gap and not a hedge - a suite total qualified by an assembly word, as in the ledger's historical 35 architecture tests passed, is not recognised as a total. That is EX-56. Second, this rule cannot tell a stale log from a current one, which is EX-54.

rules.statement: Every relevant unit in the product graph carries a two-line Broiler Code Assurance annotation immediately above its declaration. A code unit is any member that can carry executable code, and any `const` or `static readonly` field declaration that carries an initializer. Relevance is decided by one declared exemption predicate, `AssuranceScanner.ExemptionFor`; a unit that predicate does not exempt and that carries no parsed block is named, whether the block was never written, written below the declaration instead of above it, or written as half a block. The covered set is every `*.cs` file under a product project directory except the files in that project own `bin` and `obj` directories.
rules.evidence: The three product assemblies' source, as the generator would leave it, against `AssuranceScanner.ExemptionFor` and the annotation parser
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 496 relevant units and 538 exempt ones exist across 1,034 code units, so the exemption predicate answers both ways over the checkout and a clean result is a classification rather than a predicate that exempts everything. Every violating witness leaves the assurance comment IN the file, which is what makes the three worth witnessing separately: a coverage check that looked for the text rather than for the attachment would pass all of them. The two accepting witnesses carry the other half - six units the predicate covers and one per-unit escape hatch - because a rule that named every unannotated unit regardless of the predicate would be a rule about comments rather than about review. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the exemption predicate decides relevance, so a unit it wrongly exempts is invisible to this rule. The rule cannot report a unit it was told not to look at. That is why the predicate is one page in one place rather than several hundred hand-written EXEMPT lines, and why it is the reviewable artefact of the whole scheme rather than an implementation detail of it. That is EX-62. Three cases of it were too broad and were narrowed here, each with a witness of its own: case 2 asked only that the right-hand side of an assignment be SOME parameter of the constructor, so every permutation of a constructor body was exempt and exchanging two ceilings in `VmReadBounds` was invisible; case 3 accepted any argument that was a name or a constant, so a delegation supplying the LEB128 width or the budget dimension a charge lands in was exempt and the constant it supplied was the policy; and fields were not units at all, so a `const` budget could be multiplied by sixteen with no annotation to move. A SECOND LIMIT, ALSO STATED: the covered set is a directory enumeration and not the compiler evaluated `Compile` items, so a file the project pulls in from outside its own directory ships and is examined by nothing in this group. That is EX-63.

rules.statement: Every assurance annotation in the product graph parses as two adjacent comment lines, and every field on the AI line is in its closed vocabulary: `Origin`, `IP` and `Security` from their tables, `Resources` an integer 0 to 10, `Fingerprint` either `TBF` or six uppercase hex characters, `EXEMPT` a non-empty reason stated beside no other field, and nothing the system does not define. An assurance comment that does not parse, or that is attached to no declaration, is reported as stranded rather than ignored. A `Spec` value that cites an ADR names a record that exists under `docs/adr/`.
rules.evidence: Every annotation in the three product assemblies against `AssuranceAnnotation.VocabularyProblems` and `AssuranceScanner.OrphanAnnotations`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 496 annotations are parsed and held to their vocabularies. Each closed vocabulary, each required field and each of the two malformed-exemption shapes carries a witness of its own: one witness with four bad fields would be satisfied by a check that reported the first, and three of the four vocabularies could then be deleted with the suite green. `Spec is optional` and is the only defined field that may be absent, so a rule requiring every defined field would reject the honest annotation on every unit that implements no frozen record. A block that does not parse is reported twice - once for the line that does not parse and once for the human line beneath it, which on its own opens no block - because half a block is the shape a hand-edited annotation leaves. The stranded clause has a witness whose only unit is exempt, so that the input violates this rule and not J1: a block describing a unit that is no longer there is how an annotation outlives its subject, and it is invisible to a coverage rule. The citation clause resolves the ADR NUMBER against the record set on disk and does no more: `Spec=ADR-9999 s42` is rejected because no record 9999 exists, and the section is not checked because the records carry no uniform section index. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule checks that a value is IN its vocabulary and never that it is the RIGHT member of it. An annotation downgraded from `Security=High` to `Security=None` is well formed, and the generated header and the component report are derived from the annotations, so the downgrade is republished faithfully rather than reported as staleness. Nothing mechanical here can tell a correct assessment from a false one; the rubric that would decide it is prose in the component specification and the decision it asks for is a review. That is EX-65.

rules.statement: Every recorded AI fingerprint, as read from disk, equals the one the current declaration produces, and no human fingerprint names a version that is neither the current one nor preserved as `Previous`. The placeholder `TBF` is reported as its own fact, separately from a value that is simply wrong. A per-unit `EXEMPT=` annotation records no fingerprint and is not required to.
rules.evidence: Every annotated unit in the three product assemblies, scanned from the files as read from disk, against `AssuranceFingerprint.Of` over the declaration's token texts
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 496 annotated units each record a fingerprint the generator filled, and after a generation none records the placeholder - which is asserted, so the clean direction is not satisfied by a tree that has never been generated. The comparison reads the units AS THEY ARE ON DISK. Reading the generator output made this rule vacuous in its clean direction: every `Fingerprint` field there has already been rewritten to the recomputed value, so the rule compared a recomputed value against itself and editing a literal inside an annotated body left it green. Like J5 currency half it therefore runs in gate mode only, because a write run exists to refresh a fingerprint the code has outrun and asserting the pre-write value equalled the post-write value would fail every generation for a reason no reader could act on. The well-formedness assertion beside it reaches only units carrying a full assessment: an `EXEMPT=` line records no fingerprint, the specification documents that, J1 witnesses it being accepted, and applying the assertion to every annotated unit made the documented escape hatch unusable anywhere in the product tree. A `Previous=` fingerprint is accepted, because it is history and not a live approval; reporting it would punish the generator for recording what the policy requires it to record, and would push a reviewer towards deleting the history to get a green suite. The witness fingerprint is baked into the test rather than derived from the witness, because a witness that computed the value it is supposed to record would agree with itself whatever the fingerprinter did; the baked constant is asserted against the fingerprinter in the same test, so a change to normalization fails there and names it rather than quietly making four witnesses vacuous. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: six hex characters are 24 bits. The value answers whether this unit changed since it was reviewed and nothing else. It is not a collision-free identifier across units - a component with a few thousand units expects same-value pairs by the birthday bound - and it is not a cryptographic commitment: a party who can choose the code can find a preimage for a 24-bit prefix by brute force in seconds. Detecting a hostile rewrite that preserves the prefix is the job of the git history and the review event, not of this number. That is EX-61.

rules.statement: No unit is `VERIFIED` and no unit names a reviewer - live, or preserved as `Previous` - unless a human line in the source says so, and no generated artefact carries a human line reading anything but `PENDING`. The generator refuses, by exception, to rewrite a human line outside the four defined shapes at all, and to write any reviewer identifier the line it is reading does not already carry.
rules.evidence: Every annotated unit and every generated artefact against `AssuranceGenerator.RefuseInventedApproval` and the state machine
rules.nonVacuousWhen: 496 annotated units exist and every one of them reads `PENDING`, which is the honest state of this component and which the rule must not reject. Four generator transitions are witnessed separately - PENDING stays PENDING, an approval that left TBF is filled, a review the code has outrun becomes STALE with its reviewer and its approved version preserved, and a STALE line is not cleared by a recomputation - because the policy's forbidden edge is STALE straight to VERIFIED and one witness would pin only whichever branch fired first. The refusal is an exception rather than a report, so a bug that reached for a name fails loudly instead of quietly manufacturing an approval nobody gave, and it is driven THROUGH `DesiredSource` by a witness of its own rather than only by a direct call: the earlier witness called the guard directly, which pinned the function and not its wiring, so deleting its one call site left the suite green and the guard unreachable during a real generation. The shape clause is the other half of the same repair. A human body of `PENDING; Fingerprint=TBF` named nobody on either side of the name comparison, because the comparison skipped the reserved word wherever it appeared, while the annotation reader wanted exact equality and handed the head token back as a reviewer identifier - so a write run filled the fingerprint, resolved the unit to VERIFIED and published a human review of a line naming no human. Only the exact body `PENDING` now names nobody, and a body outside the four defined shapes is refused before anything is rewritten. The artefact half is asserted on the RENDERED text and not on the model: a defect that produced the right unit state and the wrong line would be invisible to a check that read only the model. The witnesses carry the identifier WITNESS-ONLY, which appears nowhere outside that directory, because a rule about false approvals cannot be witnessed without an input containing one. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule refuses a name the tooling produced. It cannot refuse a name a human typed for someone else, or an invented one that reads plausibly - the same limit rule H4 records for the attestation. The policy answers it outside the source, in the pull-request history, and nothing in this component reads that history.

rules.statement: Every generated file header and `CODE-ASSURANCE.md` is byte-identical to what the generator would produce from the annotations currently in the tree, and the component report's own figures - human reviewed, VERIFIED, unverified, and the plain statement that nothing has been reviewed - are true of the unit set it was generated from. No covered file carries more than one generated assurance block.
rules.evidence: The 45 covered product source files and `CODE-ASSURANCE.md` against `AssuranceGenerator.Plan`, and the report's own rows against `AssuranceSummary.Of`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: Forty-six artefacts are in the plan: one per covered product source file, plus the component report. The currency comparison is one function, `AssuranceGenerator.StaleArtefacts`, asserted here and by the generator harness and witnessed by a deliberately stale artefact written to a real file and read back - the clause that gates the checkout previously had no witness at all, because every other J5 witness compares a string the test is holding against its own regeneration. The comparison is byte-identical, because 'equivalent' is what a stale summary always claims to be, and because the policy forbids a hand-maintained figure such as Human-reviewed: 47/47 outright. The currency half runs in gate mode only: under BROILER_ASSURANCE_WRITE=1 the same plan is being applied by the generator harness, and asserting that the pre-write text equals the post-write text would fail every generation for a reason no reader could act on. All twelve witnesses run in both modes, so the rule is never a no-op. The report's figures are checked separately against the units they were computed from, because a byte comparison catches a report that has gone stale and cannot catch a generator that would compute a wrong figure and write it consistently - and the figure that matters most here is the one saying nothing has been reviewed. One witness covers a hand-written SPDX pair with no generated marker under it, which is the shape every file in this component was in before its first generation and the shape that published the licence declaration twice. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: there is no CI lane in this component. The policy assigns fingerprint maintenance and summary generation to CI and makes the check a release gate; here the generator and the gate are the same code run as a test, and nothing external compels either mode. A developer who does not run the suite is stopped by nothing. That is EX-60. A SECOND LIMIT: no rule pins the INVOCATION of the currency comparison over the real tree. The function is witnessed and the two call sites both use it, so neither can drift from the other, and a patch deleting both call sites at once removes the gate with nothing red. That is EX-64. The duplicate-block clause is stated separately from the byte comparison because a second summary block below the first used to survive regeneration verbatim and become a fixed point, and because the byte difference it now produces does not say what is wrong: the fact a reader needs is that the file carries two summaries and one of them is a forgery.

rules.statement: No covered product source file contains any preprocessor directive - conditional or not - and the scanner parses every covered file with the conditional symbols the build defines.
rules.evidence: The 45 covered product source files against `AssuranceSources.DirectiveViolations` over the parse, and `AssuranceSources.ParseOptions`
rules.nonVacuousWhen: The product tree contains zero preprocessor directives, so the prohibition costs nothing to adopt and the clean direction is a fact about 45 files rather than a vacuous quantifier over none. The rule exists because a directive is TRIVIA, and trivia is what the fingerprint excludes so that a formatter cannot invalidate a review: parsed with no symbol defined, a `#if NET10_0_OR_GREATER` region the build COMPILES becomes disabled text, so a backdoor could be added to an annotated method with its recorded fingerprint unmoved, and a whole public method could ship outside the unit set entirely. That is the fingerprint's central claim - a semantically relevant change must invalidate - failing outright rather than a 24-bit collision. Two defences answer it and they are deliberately independent, each with its own clause and its own witness: the parse now defines a superset of what the SDK defines for net10.0 in both configurations, so a region that ships is scanned, annotated and fingerprinted like any other code and the witness asserts that no disabled text survives the parse; and this rule refuses the directive outright, with one witness for a conditional region - both its opening and its closing directive are named, because a rule reporting only the `#if` would accept a file whose region was opened where it could not see - and one for a `#pragma`, because the rule is about the whole class of directives and not about `#if`. THE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: this rule reads the same corpus J1 does, so a compiled file outside the scanned set carries any directive it likes and is examined by nothing. That is EX-63. The symbol list is also a list: a target framework added later defines symbols this list does not, and the prohibition is what covers that gap rather than the list.
